description: Reviewed plain-English word explanations for Genesis chapter 1, keyed by Strong's ID. Meanings depend on verse context; the original Hebrew corpus and legacy dictionary remain intact.

entries.H7225: The beginning—the starting point of what happens. Here, it introduces God's creation of the heavens and the earth.
entries.H1254: To create or bring something into being. Here, God is the one doing the creating.
entries.H430: God. This Hebrew word can also refer to gods in other settings, but here it names the one God who creates.
entries.H853: A little Hebrew marker that points to the thing receiving an action. It usually has no separate English word.
entries.H8064: The heavens or sky—everything above the earth. Here it belongs to the whole created world.
entries.H776: The earth or land—the ground and the world people live on. The surrounding sentence tells you which sense fits.
entries.H1961: To be, become, or happen. In this chapter it can mean 'was,' 'came to be,' or 'let there be,' depending on the sentence.
entries.H8414: Wild, empty, or without shape. Here the earth is not yet arranged as a place ready for life.
entries.H922: Empty or unfilled. Paired with the previous word, it describes a world not yet made ready for living things.
entries.H2822: Darkness—the absence of light. Here darkness covers the deep before God calls light into being.
entries.H5921: On, over, above, or upon. This word shows where something is in relation to something else.
entries.H6440: Face, front, or surface. Here it means the surface of the deep or the waters, not a person's face.
entries.H8415: The deep—the great watery depths. Here it describes the waters before the world is ordered.
entries.H7307: Wind, breath, or spirit. Here it is used for the Spirit of God moving over the waters.
entries.H7363: To hover or move gently over something, like a bird fluttering over its young. Here it describes movement over the waters.
entries.H4325: Water or waters. Here it means the waters covering the earth before land appears.
entries.H559: To say, speak, or tell somebody something. Here God speaks and creation responds.
entries.H216: Light—what makes things visible. Here it is the light God calls into being.
entries.H7200: To see, look at, or notice. Here God sees what he has made.
entries.H3588: Because, that, when, or indeed. It's a connecting word; its English meaning depends on the sentence.
entries.H2896: Good, pleasing, or fitting. Here God calls what he has made good.
entries.H914: To separate or set things apart. Here God divides light from darkness and other parts of creation.
entries.H996: Between—showing the space or difference separating two things.
entries.H7121: To call, name, or announce. Here God gives names to parts of creation.
entries.H3117: Day—the daylight hours or a whole day, depending on the sentence.
entries.H3915: Night—the dark part of the day when the sun is not shining.
entries.H6153: Evening—the time when daylight fades and night begins.
entries.H1242: Morning—the time when night gives way to daylight.
entries.H259: One, a single thing, or the first in a count. Here it helps count the creation days.
entries.H7549: A wide space or expanse. Here it describes the sky stretching above the earth.
entries.H8432: The middle or inside of something. Here it means within the waters.
entries.H6213: To do, make, or carry something out. Here God makes parts of the created world.
entries.H834: Which, that, who, or what. It connects a description to the person or thing being described.
entries.H3651: So, thus, or in that way. Here it confirms that what God said happened.
entries.H8145: Second—the number two in an order.
entries.H6960: To gather or collect things together. Here the waters gather into one place.
entries.H413: To or toward someone or something.
entries.H4725: A place or location where something belongs.
entries.H3004: Dry ground or dry land, as opposed to water.
entries.H3220: Sea or a large body of water.
entries.H1876: To sprout or bring forth new growth. Here the earth begins producing plants.
entries.H1877: Grass, green plants, or fresh vegetation.
entries.H6212: Plants or herbs—green growth coming up from the ground.
entries.H2232: To sow or scatter seed for growing.
entries.H2233: Seed—the part of a plant that can grow into another plant.
entries.H6086: Tree or wood. Here it refers to growing trees.
entries.H6529: Fruit—the part of a tree or plant that grows and may contain seed.
entries.H3318: To go out, come out, or bring something forth. Here it describes what the earth produces.
entries.H7992: Third—the number three in an order.
entries.H3974: A light or light-giving object. Here it means the lights in the sky.
entries.H226: A sign or marker that points to something. Here the lights mark times and seasons.
entries.H4150: An appointed time or season—a set time for something to happen.
entries.H215: To shine or give light. Here the heavenly lights shine on the earth.
entries.H8147: Two, or a pair of things counted together. Here it refers to two great lights.
entries.H1419: Great, large, or important. Here it describes the larger light.
entries.H6996: Small or little. Here it describes the smaller light.
entries.H3556: Star—a light seen in the night sky.
entries.H5414: To give, put, or place something somewhere. Here God sets the lights in the sky.
entries.H4910: To rule, govern, or be in charge of something. Here the lights govern day and night.
entries.H7243: Fourth—the number four in an order.
entries.H8317: To swarm or move about in great numbers. Here the waters teem with living creatures.
entries.H8318: A swarm or mass of moving creatures.
entries.H5315: A living being or creature. In other contexts it can mean a person or life itself.
entries.H2416: Living, alive, or full of life.
entries.H8577: A great sea creature or large creature of the deep. Here it refers to creatures God makes in the waters.
entries.H3605: All, every, or the whole of something.
entries.H7430: To creep, move about, or crawl.
entries.H3671: A wing—the part a bird uses to fly.
entries.H1288: To bless—to give good things and the ability to thrive. Here God blesses living creatures.
entries.H6509: To bear fruit, have offspring, or become fruitful.
entries.H7235: To grow many, increase, or multiply.
entries.H4390: To fill something up. Here living creatures fill the waters and the earth.
entries.H2549: Fifth—the number five in an order.
entries.H929: Animals or cattle, especially larger land animals.
entries.H127: Ground or soil—the earth beneath our feet.
entries.H120: A human being or humankind. Here it refers to people God creates.
entries.H6754: An image or likeness—a representation of someone. Here it describes humanity made in God's image.
entries.H1823: A likeness or resemblance—being like someone in a particular way.
entries.H7287: To rule or have authority over. Here people are given responsibility over living creatures.
entries.H3533: To bring under control or subdue. Here people are told to bring the earth under their care.
entries.H2009: Look! See! A word used to call attention to something important.
entries.H3966: Very, greatly, or exceedingly. Here God sees that creation is very good.
entries.H8345: Sixth—the number six in an order.
entries.H4723: A gathered place or collection of water. Here it means the bodies of water God calls seas.
entries.H4327: A kind, type, or family. Here it groups plants and living creatures according to their kinds.
entries.H4475: Rule, authority, or the place where someone has charge. Here it describes the work of the lights in the sky.
